g.text: The per-neuron function that runs after the weighted sum —
and the reason “deep learning” is allowed to be deep.
STEP · SIGMOID · TANH · RELU + THE MSE DERIVATIVE

div.style: font-size:23px; line-height:1.45; color:#1f1a14; font-style:italic; font-family:Fraunces, Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: Without a non-linear activation between layers, stacking depth buys you nothing — the whole network collapses algebraically to a single linear layer. The activation function is what makes deep learning deep.

svg.text: § 01 — THE FOUR ACTIVATIONS, SIDE BY SIDE

g.text: W₂·(W₁·x + b₁) + b₂ = (W₂·W₁)·x + (W₂·b₁ + b₂) = W′·x + b′
→ two layers collapse algebraically to one. Depth is decorative.
W₂ · ReLU(W₁·x + b₁) + b₂ ← cannot be folded into one matmul
→ depth is real. The ReLU breaks the algebra.
§ 03 — THE MENU THE LECTURER NEVER WROTE
ReLU unless you have a specific reason.
what’s on the final layer · match to task

text.tspan: Sigmoid is for binary classification only.

g.text: trick will produce a broken classifier.
x → W·x + b → activation → ŷ → J(ŷ, y)
BACKWARD PASS ← propagate gradients via chain rule
iteration = one forward + one backward + one update · epoch = N / batch_size iterations · batch_size is yours to choose
Three rules, three corrections, two ships
① Activations introduce non-linearity. Without them, depth collapses.
② Hidden ≠ output. Pick hidden by depth-stability; pick output by task.
③ Backprop is the chain rule applied layer by layer. Same math, more layers.
① Sigmoid is for binary classification only. Use softmax for multi-class — not threshold bands.
② ReLU is the hidden-layer default, not “the regression activation.” Regression output is the identity.
③ Step is “outdated” because it’s non-differentiable — that’s the mechanism, not just the verdict.
predict(x) = activate( weightedSum(x) ) ; activate = step | sigmoid | tanh | ReLU | softmax | identity
